examples.ko: 이 측정기로 방의 온도를 재 봐요.
examples.en: I measure the room temperature with this instrument.
At the hospital they checked me with a blood pressure monitor.

examples.ko: 새로 산 측정기가 고장 나서 바꿔 왔어요.
examples.en: The new meter I bought broke, so I exchanged it.
The red light came on on the fine dust meter.

examples.ko: 측정기 사용법을 모르면 설명서를 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: If you don't know how to use the meter, read the manual.

examples.ko: 아버지가 사 오신 측정기는 작고 가벼워요.
examples.en: The meter my father bought is small and light.

explain: 온도계, 체중계, 혈압계처럼 재는 도구 이름에는 '-계'가 많이 붙고, '-기'는 기계 느낌이 강한 도구에 붙어요. 보통 '미세먼지 측정기'처럼 재는 대상을 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
explain_en: Measuring tools often end in '-계' (온도계, 체중계, 혈압계), while '-기' suggests more of a machine. Koreans usually put what is being measured in front, as in '미세먼지 측정기' (fine dust meter).

examples.ko: 할머니 집 뒤에 작은 텃밭이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small vegetable plot behind my grandmother's house.
Every weekend I grow lettuce in my garden plot.
I watered the plot and pulled the weeds too.
The tomatoes in our garden plot have ripened red.

examples.ko: 아파트 옥상에 텃밭을 만든 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people have even made a vegetable garden on an apartment rooftop.

examples.ko: 직접 기른 텃밭 채소라서 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes better because the vegetables come from my own plot.

explain: '밭'은 채소나 곡식을 키우는 땅 전체를 부르지만, '텃밭'은 집 가까이에 있는 작은 밭이에요. 팔려고 키우기보다 가족이 먹으려고 키우는 느낌이 있어서 '주말농장'과도 가까워요.
explain_en: '밭' covers any field, while '텃밭' is a small plot near the house. It suggests growing food for your own family rather than to sell, which is close to the idea of a '주말농장' (weekend farm).

examples.ko: 비 때문에 창문에 판자를 대 놓았어요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, I boarded up the window.
The man cut a plank and made a bookshelf.

examples.ko: 산비탈에 낡은 판자로 지은 집이 아직 몇 채 남아 있어요.
examples.en: A few houses built of old boards still remain on the hillside.

examples.ko: 판자가 썩어서 이 다리는 건너기 위험해요.
examples.en: The boards are rotten, so this bridge is dangerous to cross.
This board is thick and hard, so it is sturdy.

examples.ko: 마당 한쪽에 남은 판자를 쌓아 두었어요.
examples.en: I stacked the leftover planks in one corner of the yard.

explain: 얇고 넓게 자른 나무가 '판자'이고, 두껍고 긴 나무는 '각목'이라고 해서 모양으로 이름이 갈려요. '판자촌'은 낡은 판자로 지은 집이 모인 동네를 가리키는 말로 옛날 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A '판자' is a thin, wide cut of wood, while a thick, long piece is called a '각목'. The word '판자촌' (shanty town) comes up often in stories about the past.

examples.en: My grandfather was diagnosed with liver cancer.
Liver cancer shows almost no symptoms in the early stage.

examples.ko: 간암 수술을 받은 환자가 잘 회복하고 있어요.
examples.en: The patient who had liver cancer surgery is recovering well.

examples.ko: 의사가 간암 검사를 받아 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to get tested for liver cancer.

examples.ko: 간암을 일찍 찾으려면 정기 검진이 중요해요.
examples.en: Regular checkups are important to find liver cancer early.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 간암 치료법이 새로 나왔다고 해요.
examples.en: The news says a new treatment for liver cancer has appeared.

explain: 몸의 부위 뒤에 '암'을 붙이면 병 이름이 돼요. '위암', '폐암', '대장암'처럼요. 보통 '간암에 걸리다', '간암 진단을 받다'로 말하고, 무거운 병이라 가볍게 농담하는 말에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Adding '암' (cancer) after an organ name makes a disease name, as in '위암', '폐암', '대장암'. People say '간암에 걸리다' (get liver cancer) or '간암 진단을 받다', and the word is not used lightly in jokes.

examples.en: Cats are nimble, so they jump high.
That player dodged the ball nimbly.
I like the shoes with the sleek design.
He is big but quick on his feet.

examples.ko: 어제 본 축구 선수는 정말 날렵했어요.
examples.en: The soccer player I saw yesterday was really agile.
The new car's front looks sleek.

explain: '날쌔다'는 움직임이 아주 빠를 때 쓰고, '날렵하다'는 움직임에 더해 몸매나 모양이 군더더기 없이 깔끔할 때까지 써요. 그래서 사람과 동물의 몸 말고도 구두, 자동차 같은 물건의 모양에도 써요.
explain_en: '날쌔다' is for very fast movement, while '날렵하다' adds a sense of a lean, clean shape. So it works for bodies and also for the look of things like shoes and cars.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 도랑에 물이 가득 차요.
examples.en: When it rains, the ditch fills with water.
The kids caught frogs in the ditch.
My shoes got wet while crossing the ditch.
The stream in front of the village is clear and cool.

examples.ko: 아버지가 도랑 옆에 작은 길을 만들었어요.
examples.en: My father made a small path beside the ditch.

examples.ko: 낙엽 때문에 도랑이 막혀서 물이 넘쳤어요.
examples.en: Fallen leaves blocked the ditch and the water overflowed.

explain: '강'과 '개울'보다 작고, '도랑'은 사람이 물을 대거나 빼려고 판 좁은 물길일 때가 많아요. 도시에서는 '하수구'를 더 흔하게 쓰고, '도랑'은 시골 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 도랑 치고 가재 잡는다더니, 청소하다가 잃어버린 반지도 찾았어요.
phrases.en: Clean the ditch and catch a crayfish too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일을 하다가 뜻밖에 다른 이득까지 얻을 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb used when doing one task brings an unexpected extra benefit.
phrases.en_equiv: kill two birds with one stone

explain_en: It is smaller than a '강' or '개울', and a '도랑' is often a narrow channel dug to bring in or drain water. In cities people say '하수구' more, while '도랑' shows up in countryside stories.

examples.en: I got angry because my younger brother hogged the game console.

examples.ko: 한 사람이 인기를 독차지하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: One person shouldn't take all the popularity.
My older brother took the whole sofa for himself.

examples.ko: 그 영화가 올해 상을 독차지할 거예요.
examples.en: That movie will sweep the awards this year.
There were no customers, so I sat with the whole shop to myself.
Please don't dominate the conversation by yourself.

explain: '혼자 차지하다'와 비슷하지만 '독차지하다'에는 남이 나눠 가져야 할 몫까지 혼자 갖는다는 불만의 느낌이 있어요. 사랑, 인기, 상, 자리처럼 나눌 수 있는 것에 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '혼자 차지하다' (take for oneself), but '독차지하다' carries a note of complaint that someone is taking a share meant for others. It often goes with love, popularity, prizes and seats.

examples.en: I argued with my friend over a small matter.
The couple often argue about money.

examples.ko: 말다툼하다가 서로 말을 안 하게 됐어요.
examples.en: We argued and ended up not speaking to each other.
I had a quarrel with my brother and went into my room.

examples.ko: 길에서 두 사람이 크게 말다툼하고 있어요.
examples.en: Two people are having a loud argument on the street.

examples.ko: 말다툼할 때는 목소리를 낮추는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to lower your voice when you argue.

explain: '싸우다'는 주먹이 오가는 싸움까지 넓게 쓰지만 '말다툼하다'는 말로만 다투는 거예요. 더 가볍게 티격태격하는 것은 '티격태격하다'라고 해요. '말다툼을 하다'로 풀어서 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: '싸우다' can include physical fights, but '말다툼하다' is a quarrel in words only. A lighter bickering is '티격태격하다'. You can also split it as '말다툼을 하다'.

examples.en: I put red nail polish on my nails.
My nail polish is chipped, so I have to redo it.

examples.ko: 주말에 친구와 같이 매니큐어를 사러 갔어요.
examples.en: On the weekend I went with a friend to buy nail polish.
This nail polish dries quickly, so it's convenient.
You can't wear nail polish at school.

examples.ko: 매니큐어 냄새가 너무 독해서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: The nail polish smell was so strong that I opened the window.

explain: 한국어 '매니큐어'는 손톱에 칠하는 물감 자체를 가리켜요. 발톱에 하는 것은 '페디큐어'라고 하고, 동사는 '바르다'나 '칠하다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '네일'이라는 말도 많이 들려요.
explain_en: In Korean '매니큐어' means the nail polish itself. For toenails people say '페디큐어', and the verbs are '바르다' or '칠하다'. In daily talk you also hear the word '네일'.

en: force of flowing water; speed of flowing water

examples.en: It rained a lot, so the current got stronger.
Swimming against the current is really hard.

examples.ko: 이 강은 물살이 느려서 배 타기 좋아요.
examples.en: This river has a slow current, so it's good for boating.
The child almost got swept away by the current.

examples.ko: 다리 아래로 물살 소리가 시원하게 들려요.
examples.en: The sound of the rushing water under the bridge is refreshing.

examples.ko: 낚시꾼이 빠른 물살을 피해 자리를 잡았어요.
examples.en: The angler picked a spot away from the fast current.

explain: '물살'은 흐르는 물의 힘과 빠르기에 초점이 있어서 '물살이 세다', '빠르다', '느리다'로 말해요. 가만히 있는 물에는 쓰지 않아요. 바다에서 크게 일어나는 움직임은 '파도'라고 해요.
explain_en: '물살' focuses on the force and speed of moving water, so you say '물살이 세다/빠르다/느리다'. It is not used for still water. The big motions at sea are called '파도' (waves).

examples.en: I put a banana and milk in the blender and blended them.
The blender was so loud that the baby woke up.
I blend fruit in the blender to make juice.

examples.ko: 새 믹서를 사고 싶은데 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: I want to buy a new blender, so please recommend one.
Close the blender lid and press the button.
The blender gets louder when you add ice.

explain: 집에서 과일이나 채소를 가는 기계는 '블렌더'보다 '믹서'라고 부르는 일이 더 익숙해요. 보통 '믹서에 갈다', '믹서로 갈다'처럼 '갈다'와 같이 쓰고, 반죽을 섞는 기계와는 달라요.
explain_en: For the kitchen machine that grinds fruit or vegetables, Koreans are used to calling it a '믹서' rather than a 'blender'. It usually goes with '갈다' (to grind), as in '믹서에 갈다'.

examples.ko: 큰 소리로 통화하면 다른 사람에게 민폐예요.
examples.en: Talking loudly on the phone is a nuisance to others.

examples.ko: 지하철에서 큰 가방을 메면 민폐일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Carrying a big bag on the subway can be a nuisance.
I came late and caused trouble for the team.

examples.ko: 친구한테 민폐가 될까 봐 부탁을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't ask because I was afraid of troubling my friend.

examples.ko: 길을 막고 사진을 찍는 건 민폐 행동이에요.
examples.en: Blocking the road to take photos is inconsiderate behavior.
I'm careful not to bother my neighbors.

explain: 부탁하거나 사과할 때는 '폐를 끼치다'가 더 흔하고, '민폐'는 '그건 민폐예요'처럼 행동을 평가하는 말로 많이 써요. '민폐 행동'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙이기도 해요. 남에게 불편을 주는 일이라 가볍게 지적할 때도 써요.
explain_en: When asking a favor or apologizing, '폐를 끼치다' is more common, while '민폐' is often used to judge behavior, as in '그건 민폐예요'. It can take a word after it, like '민폐 행동'.

examples.en: The company paid compensation to the victim.
I was due to receive compensation because of the accident.
How much the damages will be hasn't been decided yet.
The court ruled that a large sum in damages be paid.
I took out a loan to raise the money for the damages.

examples.ko: 보험으로 배상금 일부를 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can pay part of the damages with insurance.

explain: '배상금'은 잘못으로 남에게 끼친 손해를 돈으로 갚을 때 쓰고, 비슷한 '보상금'은 적법한 일로 생긴 손해나 수고를 돈으로 줄 때 써요. 도로 공사로 땅을 내놓고 받는 돈은 '보상금'이에요.
explain_en: '배상금' is money paid for harm caused by a fault, while the similar '보상금' is money given for a loss from a lawful act. Money you get for giving up land for a road is '보상금'.

examples.en: The soldier raised a white flag and surrendered.

examples.ko: 흰 천을 백기처럼 흔들어 신호를 보냈어요.
examples.en: I waved a white cloth like a white flag to signal.
They fought until the other side raised the white flag.
Our team finally gave up.
A white flag is a sign that you will stop fighting.

examples.ko: 전쟁 영화에서 백기가 나오는 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a scene with a white flag in a war movie.

explain: '백기'는 거의 '백기를 들다'로 쓰여요. 진짜 깃발 이야기가 아니어도 '포기하다'의 가벼운 말로 써요. 비슷한 '손들다'는 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 숙제가 너무 많아서 결국 백기를 들었어요.
phrases.en: to raise the white flag; to give up
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸움이나 경쟁에서 졌다고 인정하거나, 어려운 일을 포기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when admitting defeat in a fight or competition, or giving up on something hard.

explain_en: '백기' appears almost always as '백기를 들다'. Even when no real flag is involved, it works as a lighter way of saying '포기하다'. The similar '손들다' is a more casual daily expression.

examples.en: I saw a polar bear for the first time at the zoo.
Polar bears live on the ice.

examples.ko: 얼음이 녹아서 북극곰이 살 곳이 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: The ice is melting, so the places polar bears can live are shrinking.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 북극곰 인형을 안고 자요.
examples.en: My child sleeps hugging a polar bear doll.
I watched a video of a polar bear swimming underwater.

examples.ko: 흰 털 때문에 북극곰은 눈 속에서 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: Because of its white fur, a polar bear is hard to see in the snow.

explain: 곰 이름은 사는 곳이나 모습을 붙인 것이 많아요. '불곰', '반달가슴곰'처럼요. 북극곰은 지구 온난화 이야기가 나올 때 환경 뉴스에 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Many bear names add where they live or how they look, like '불곰' (brown bear) and '반달가슴곰' (Asian black bear). '북극곰' often appears in environment news about global warming.

examples.en: The plane made a forced landing because of engine trouble.
The news of the forced landing was on the news.
Luckily everyone was safe in the forced landing accident.
The fuel ran out, so a forced landing was unavoidable.
The place of the forced landing was near the sea.
I watched a movie about a spaceship's forced landing.

explain: '불시착'은 계획한 공항이 아닌 곳에 어쩔 수 없이 내리는 일이라 그냥 '착륙'과는 달라요. 비슷한 '비상착륙'은 문제가 생겨 급히 내리는 일 전체에 쓰고, 불시착은 예정에 없던 곳에 내렸다는 점이 두드러져요.
explain_en: A '불시착' is landing at an unplanned place out of necessity, so it differs from an ordinary '착륙'. The similar '비상착륙' covers any urgent landing, while '불시착' stresses landing somewhere that wasn't planned.

en: make an emergency landing; make a forced landing

examples.en: The plane made a forced landing on a small island.
In the movie, a spaceship crash-lands on a strange planet.
Where should you make an emergency landing if the engine stops?
There was an accident in which a helicopter made a forced landing in the mountains.

examples.ko: 불시착한 뒤에도 승객들은 침착하게 구조를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: Even after the forced landing, the passengers waited calmly for rescue.
Because of the blizzard, we nearly had to make a forced landing.

explain: '불시착하다'는 '-에 불시착하다'처럼 내린 곳에 '에'를 써요. 정상으로 내리는 '착륙하다'와 달리 고장이나 날씨 때문에 예정과 다르게 내렸다는 느낌이 들어 있어요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: You mark the place with '에', as in '-에 불시착하다'. Unlike the ordinary '착륙하다', it implies landing differently from plan because of a breakdown or weather. It is common in news reports.

examples.en: The hunter went up the mountain with his hunting dog.

examples.ko: 이 사냥개는 냄새를 아주 잘 맡아요.
examples.en: This hound has a very good sense of smell.
The hound ran off chasing a rabbit.

examples.ko: 옆집 사냥개는 낯선 사람을 보면 짖어요.
examples.en: The neighbor's hunting dog barks when it sees a stranger.

examples.ko: 사냥개를 훈련시키는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to train a hunting dog.
The hunting dog in the movie is really cool.

explain: 일하는 개 이름은 '사냥개', '경찰견', '안내견'처럼 '-개'와 '-견'이 섞여 있어서 따로 익히는 게 좋아요. '권력의 사냥개'처럼 쓰면 시키는 대로만 움직이는 사람을 낮춰 부르는 말이 되기도 해요.
explain_en: Names for working dogs mix '-개' and '-견', as in '사냥개', '경찰견', '안내견', so it's best to learn each one. In a phrase like '권력의 사냥개' (a hound of power), it can put down someone who just does as told.

examples.en: A blue sapphire is set in the engagement ring.
Sapphires are usually blue.
My grandmother passed down a sapphire necklace to me.
I received sapphire earrings as a gift from a friend.

examples.ko: 이 사파이어는 크기가 커서 값이 비싸요.
examples.en: This sapphire is large, so it's expensive.
The birthstone for people born in September is the sapphire.

explain: '사파이어'는 파란색이 대표적이라 '사파이어 블루'처럼 색 이름으로도 써요. 붉은 보석인 '루비'와 짝으로 같이 나올 때가 많아요. 서양에서 들어온 보석 이름은 대부분 외래어 그대로 써요.
explain_en: Blue is the typical color, so '사파이어' is also used as a color name, as in '사파이어 블루'. It often appears as a pair with the red gem '루비' (ruby). Gem names that came from the West are mostly used as loanwords.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 삼림이 잘 보존되어 있어요.
examples.en: The forests in this region are well preserved.
A lot of forest was lost to the wildfire.

examples.ko: 삼림을 지키려면 나무를 함부로 베면 안 돼요.
examples.en: To protect the forest, you must not cut trees carelessly.
I breathed clean air in the woods.
Many animals live in forest areas.

examples.ko: 삼림 자원을 아껴 쓰는 일이 중요해요.
examples.en: Using forest resources carefully is important.

explain: 일상에서 쓰는 순우리말은 '숲'이고, '삼림'은 뉴스나 교과서에서 넓은 숲을 말할 때 쓰는 한자어예요. 산책하며 말할 때는 '숲'이 자연스러워요. '산림'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: The everyday native word is '숲', while '삼림' is a Sino-Korean word used in news and textbooks for large woodlands. On a walk, '숲' sounds natural. '산림' is used in almost the same way.

examples.ko: 우리 세 친구는 학교에서 삼총사로 불려요.
examples.en: The three of us are called the trio at school.

examples.ko: 삼총사 이야기를 읽어 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever read the story of the Three Musketeers?
I envy the trio who are always together.
Our trio meets every Friday.

examples.ko: 영화 속 삼총사의 주인공은 검을 잘 써요.
examples.en: The hero of the three musketeers in the movie is good with a sword.

examples.ko: 삼총사 중 한 명이 이사를 가서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: One of our trio moved away, which is a pity.

explain: 원래 프랑스 소설 『삼총사』에서 온 말인데, 한국어에서는 친하게 붙어 다니는 세 사람을 가리켜요. 비슷한 '삼인방'은 어떤 일을 이끄는 핵심 세 사람이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It comes from the French novel 『삼총사』 (The Three Musketeers), but in Korean it refers to three people who are always together. The similar '삼인방' feels more like the three key people leading something.

examples.en: The pine is an evergreen that stays green in winter too.

examples.ko: 학교 운동장 옆에 상록수가 줄지어 서 있어요.
examples.en: Evergreen trees stand in a row beside the school playground.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 상록수라서 일 년 내내 푸르러요.
examples.en: This tree is an evergreen, so it stays green all year.

examples.ko: 겨울에도 푸른 상록수 덕분에 산이 쓸쓸하지 않아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the evergreens, the mountain doesn't feel bleak in winter.

examples.ko: 정원에 상록수를 심으면 사계절 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: If you plant evergreens in the garden, it looks nice in every season.

examples.ko: 단풍나무는 상록수가 아니라서 가을에 잎이 떨어져요.
examples.en: Maple trees aren't evergreens, so their leaves fall in autumn.

explain: 반대말은 가을에 잎이 지는 '낙엽수'예요. 한국에서는 소나무가 대표적인 상록수이고, 『상록수』라는 유명한 소설도 있어서 이름이 낯설지 않아요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '낙엽수', a tree that sheds its leaves in autumn. In Korea the pine is the typical evergreen, and there is a famous novel called 『상록수』, so the word is familiar.

examples.en: A small bird is singing inside the birdcage.

examples.ko: 새장 문을 열어 두었더니 새가 날아갔어요.
examples.en: I left the birdcage door open and the bird flew away.
I hung the birdcage by the sunny window.

examples.ko: 아이가 새장에 모이를 넣어 주고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is putting feed into the birdcage.

examples.ko: 새장이 너무 작아서 새가 불편해 보여요.
examples.en: The birdcage is so small that the bird looks uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 새장 청소는 일주일에 한 번 해요.
examples.en: I clean the birdcage once a week.

explain: '새장'은 사람이 새를 기르려고 가두는 곳이라, 새가 직접 짓는 '둥지'나 새를 위해 달아 주는 '새집'과 달라요. '새장 속의 새'처럼 자유가 없는 처지를 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: A '새장' is where people keep a bird, unlike a '둥지' (nest) that birds build or a '새집' (birdhouse) put up for them. A phrase like '새장 속의 새' figuratively describes someone without freedom.

examples.ko: 동생은 손재주가 좋아서 뭐든 잘 만들어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is good with their hands and makes anything well.
Thanks to my mother's handiwork, the house became pretty.

examples.ko: 저는 손재주가 없어서 선물 포장도 서툴러요.
examples.en: I'm not good with my hands, so I'm clumsy even at gift wrapping.
I want to use my manual skill to open a workshop.
My grandfather was a carpenter with outstanding skill.

examples.ko: 손재주 좋은 친구가 가방을 고쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: A friend who is good with their hands fixed my bag.

explain: '손재주가 있다/없다', '좋다/뛰어나다'로 말하고, 말솜씨나 머리가 좋은 것에는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 '손끝이 야무지다'는 일을 꼼꼼하고 단정하게 한다는 칭찬이고, 요리 솜씨는 따로 '손맛'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You say '손재주가 있다/없다' or '좋다/뛰어나다', and it isn't used for verbal skill or intelligence. The similar '손끝이 야무지다' praises neat, careful work, and skill in cooking is called '손맛' instead.

examples.en: The wedding hall is inside a hotel.
I gave the gift money before entering the hall.
Guests arrived at the hall one by one.
I signed the guest book at the entrance of the hall.
There is a separate bus that goes to the hall.
The hall was small, so there weren't enough seats.

explain: '식장'은 주로 결혼식을 하는 곳을 가리켜서 '결혼식장'을 줄여 부를 때가 많아요. 장례를 치르는 곳은 '장례식장'이라고 따로 말하고, 졸업식이나 시상식 장소는 보통 '강당'이나 '행사장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '식장' mostly means a wedding venue and is often a short form of '결혼식장'. A funeral venue is called '장례식장', and places for graduations or award ceremonies are usually called '강당' or '행사장'.

examples.en: My mother is thrifty and spends household money carefully.

examples.ko: 알뜰한 사람은 세일 기간에 장을 봐요.
examples.en: Thrifty people shop for groceries during the sale period.
I saved my allowance carefully and bought a bag.
My spouse and I manage the household economically.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 알뜰한 가격으로 점심을 팔아요.
examples.en: That shop sells lunch at a good, economical price.
I feel good when I'm told I'm thrifty.

explain: '아끼다'는 쓰는 것을 줄이는 행동이고, '알뜰하다'는 돈이나 물건을 헛되이 쓰지 않고 꼼꼼히 챙기는 사람의 성격에 가까워요. '구두쇠'는 인색하다고 비웃는 말이지만 '알뜰하다'는 칭찬이에요. '알뜰폰'처럼 이름에도 붙어요.
explain_en: '아끼다' is the act of cutting back, while '알뜰하다' describes a person who carefully avoids waste. '구두쇠' mocks someone as stingy, but '알뜰하다' is praise. It also appears in names like '알뜰폰' (budget phone plan).

examples.en: The match was tied, so it went into extra time.
Our team won after extra time.
If it goes to extra time, your stamina drops a lot.
The winning goal came in extra time.
If the score is still tied in extra time, there is a penalty shootout.

examples.ko: 지난 시즌에는 연장전이 많아서 선수들이 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: Last season had many extra-time games, so the players had a hard time.

explain: 정해진 시간 안에 승부가 나지 않을 때 더 하는 경기가 '연장전'이에요. 야구에서는 '연장 10회'처럼 회로 말하고, 축구에서는 연장전에서도 비기면 '승부차기'로 넘어가요.
explain_en: A '연장전' is the extra play when no winner is decided in the set time. In baseball people say '연장 10회' (the 10th inning of extras), and in soccer a tie after extra time goes to '승부차기' (penalties).

examples.en: The couple danced a waltz at their wedding.

examples.ko: 왈츠 음악이 나오자 사람들이 짝을 지었어요.
examples.en: When waltz music started, people paired up.

examples.ko: 왈츠 스텝이 어려워서 매일 연습하고 있어요.
examples.en: The waltz steps are hard, so I practice every day.
We turned slowly to an elegant waltz.
The first dance I learned was the waltz.
A slow waltz is playing on the radio.

explain: '왈츠'는 3박자 춤이라 '하나, 둘, 셋' 하고 세는 느낌으로 춰요. 동사는 '추다'를 쓰고 '왈츠를 추다'처럼 같이 말해요. '탱고', '블루스'처럼 서양 춤 이름은 대부분 외래어 그대로 써요.
explain_en: The '왈츠' is in three beats, danced with a feel of counting one-two-three. The verb is '추다', as in '왈츠를 추다'. Western dance names such as '탱고' and '블루스' are mostly used as loanwords.

examples.en: I spent my childhood in the countryside.
My childhood memories are hazy but happy.
In early childhood, kids grow up healthy by playing a lot.
I heard that writer lived abroad in childhood.
I'm still in touch with my childhood friends.
I watched a movie about childhood on the weekend.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '어린 시절'이나 '어릴 때'를 훨씬 많이 쓰고, '유년기'는 글이나 방송에서 나이를 단계로 나눌 때 써요. '유년기, 청소년기, 성인기'처럼 이어서 말해요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '어린 시절' or '어릴 때' far more, while '유년기' is used in writing and broadcasts when dividing life into stages. It lines up as '유년기, 청소년기, 성인기'.

examples.en: Our apartment complex will be rebuilt next year.
The building is old, so it needs to be rebuilt.

examples.ko: 재건축 때문에 이웃들이 모두 이사를 갔어요.
examples.en: All the neighbors moved out because of the rebuilding.
The city granted permission for the reconstruction.
Will house prices go up after the rebuilding is done?
The noise of the rebuilding work has been loud since morning.

explain: 재건축은 낡은 건물을 허물고 새로 짓는 것, '리모델링'은 건물을 그대로 두고 고치는 것이라 달라요. 한국 뉴스에서는 주로 아파트 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: '재건축' means tearing down an old building and building anew, while '리모델링' keeps the building and renovates it. In Korean news it mostly comes up in stories about apartments.

en: trickling; gently flowing (water); tagging along behind

examples.en: The stream trickles along.
The puppy follows its owner around closely.
Water is trickling out of the faucet.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 손을 잡고 졸졸 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: The child toddled along after her mother, holding her hand.

examples.ko: 작은 샘에서 맑은 물이 졸졸 솟아요.
examples.en: Clear water bubbles gently from the small spring.

examples.ko: 어린 동생이 하루 종일 졸졸 따라와요.
examples.en: My little sibling tags along behind me all day.

explain: 물이 가늘게 흐르는 소리와, 작은 아이나 동물이 계속 따라다니는 모습 두 가지에 써요. 물이 세게 흐르면 '콸콸', 많이 쏟아지면 '주룩주룩'을 써서 물의 양에 따라 말이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used both for the sound of thin water flowing and for a small child or animal following closely. Stronger flow is '콸콸' and heavy pouring is '주룩주룩', so the word changes with the amount of water.

examples.en: This weekly comes out every Monday.
Weeklies are piled up in the hospital waiting room.
My interview was published in the weekly.
My father has a regular subscription to a weekly.
Celebrity rumors are often covered in the weeklies.
These days I read weeklies on an app rather than on paper.

explain: 매일 나오면 '일간지', 매주 나오면 '주간지', 매달 나오면 '월간지'라고 해서 '-간지' 앞 글자로 주기를 구분해요. '잡지'와 가깝지만 주간지는 그 주의 소식을 다루는 내용이 많아요.
explain_en: A daily is '일간지', a weekly is '주간지' and a monthly is '월간지', so the character before '-간지' shows the cycle. It is close to a magazine, but a '주간지' often covers the week's news.

examples.en: The event organizer greeted the participants.
The organizer prepared tents in case of rain.
Who is the organizer of this gathering?

examples.ko: 주최자 측에서 입장료를 받지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The organizers decided not to charge an entrance fee.
I sent an inquiry email to the tournament organizer.
He said he would take responsibility as the organizer.

explain: 행사 안내문에서 '주최'는 행사를 열고 책임지는 쪽, '주관'은 실제로 운영하는 쪽으로 나눠 쓰기도 해요. 진행을 맡은 사람은 '사회자'나 '진행자'이고, 파티를 여는 개인은 '호스트'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: On event notices, '주최' is the side that holds the event and takes responsibility, while '주관' is the side that actually runs it. The person emceeing is a '사회자' or '진행자', and a person throwing a party is more naturally a '호스트'.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤에 길에 지렁이가 나와 있어요.
examples.en: After the rain, earthworms are out on the road.
Earthworms make the soil soft.
The child screamed on seeing an earthworm.
The angler used an earthworm as bait.

examples.ko: 정원에 지렁이가 많으면 흙이 좋은 편이에요.
examples.en: If there are many earthworms in the garden, the soil is usually good.
An earthworm is wriggling in the ground.

explain: 지렁이는 '꿈틀거리다'와 함께 자주 나오고, 비 온 뒤 길에 나온 모습으로 많이 말해요. 텃밭이나 화분의 흙을 좋게 만드는 고마운 생물로도 알려져 있어요.

phrases.example: 지렁이도 밟으면 꿈틀한다더니, 그 순한 친구가 화를 냈어요.
phrases.en: Even a worm wriggles when stepped on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무리 순하고 약한 사람도 계속 괴롭히면 화를 낸다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning even the meekest person will get angry if pushed too far.

explain_en: The word often goes with '꿈틀거리다' (to wriggle) and is mentioned mostly for worms out on the road after rain. It is also known as a helpful creature that improves soil in gardens and pots.

examples.ko: 다친 손을 깨끗한 천으로 눌러 지혈했어요.
examples.en: I pressed the injured hand with a clean cloth to stop the bleeding.
When your nose bleeds, you lower your head and stop the bleeding.
The doctor first stopped the bleeding and then stitched the wound.
If you don't stop the bleeding, the blood keeps coming.
I learned how to stop bleeding by tying with a strap.

examples.ko: 빨리 지혈해야 해서 구급대원이 붕대를 감았어요.
examples.en: The paramedic wrapped a bandage because the bleeding had to be stopped quickly.

explain: '피를 멈추다'보다 응급 상황에서 훨씬 자연스러운 말이에요. 상처를 누르거나 감싸서 피를 멈추게 하는 행동에 쓰고, 약으로 멈추는 것은 '지혈제'를 쓴다고 해요. 응급처치 교육에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It sounds far more natural in an emergency than '피를 멈추다'. It is used for pressing or wrapping a wound to stop blood, and a medicine for this is called '지혈제'. It comes up often in first aid training.

examples.en: Sprinkling sesame seeds on seasoned greens makes them nuttier.
They press sesame seeds for oil to make sesame oil.

examples.ko: 김밥 위에 참깨가 솔솔 뿌려져 있어요.
examples.en: Sesame seeds are lightly sprinkled over the gimbap.
I bought a bag of sesame seeds at the market.
The aroma of sesame gets stronger when it is toasted.
The salad with sesame dressing is delicious.

explain: '참깨'로 짠 기름이 '참기름'이고, 비슷하게 생긴 '들깨'에서는 '들기름'이 나와요. 요리할 때는 그냥 '깨'라고 줄여 말하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: Oil pressed from '참깨' is '참기름', while the similar-looking '들깨' gives '들기름'. When cooking, people often shorten it to just '깨'.

examples.en: My favorite subject is math.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에 교과목이 두 개 늘었어요.
examples.en: Two subjects were added this semester.
Each subject has a different teacher.
Which subject is the hardest?
Please check the subject timetable.
In the new subject we learn coding.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '과목'이라고 하는 일이 더 많고, '교과목'은 학교 안내문이나 시간표처럼 딱딱한 문서에서 자주 보여요. 국어, 수학, 영어 같은 하나하나를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: In daily speech people more often just say '과목', while '교과목' shows up in formal documents such as school notices and timetables. It refers to each individual subject like 국어, 수학 or 영어.

examples.en: We're in the mountains, so there is no cell tower nearby.

examples.ko: 기지국이 고장 나서 전화가 안 터져요.
examples.en: The base station broke down, so phone calls won't connect.
A new cell tower was built and the internet got faster.
The carrier decided to build more base stations.

examples.ko: 기지국 근처에 살면 전파가 강하게 잡혀요.
examples.en: If you live near a cell tower, the signal is strong.

examples.ko: 건물 옥상에 기지국 안테나가 설치되어 있어요.
examples.en: A base station antenna is installed on the rooftop.

explain: 휴대폰 신호 이야기에서 '기지국'은 '전파가 터지다', '통신망'과 함께 나와요. 안테나 하나가 아니라 신호를 받아 전달하는 시설 전체를 가리켜서 '안테나'와는 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: In talk about phone signals, '기지국' goes with '전파가 터지다' (the signal comes through) and '통신망' (network). It means the whole facility that receives and relays signals, not just one antenna, so it is kept distinct from '안테나'.

en: take care; be cautious of one's health

examples.ko: 비가 오니까 감기 안 걸리게 몸조심하세요.
examples.en: It's raining, so take care not to catch a cold.
The weather is cold, so I have to look after my health.
After surgery, it's important to take care of yourself.
Take care on your trip and come back healthy.
My grandmother always tells me to take care of myself.
The exam is next week, so I'll take care of my health.

explain: '조심하세요'가 사고나 위험 앞에서 쓰는 말이라면 '몸조심하세요'는 감기, 피로, 부상 같은 건강 문제까지 걱정하는 인사예요. 아픈 사람이나 먼 길을 떠나는 사람에게 헤어질 때 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '조심하세요' warns about accidents or danger, while '몸조심하세요' also worries about health problems like colds, fatigue and injuries. It is a common goodbye to someone who is sick or going on a long trip.

en: flare up; bristle; snap in anger

examples.en: My younger brother flared up when his friend teased him.
He is the type to bristle at even small remarks.

examples.ko: 그는 비판을 듣고 발끈해서 자리를 떴어요.
examples.en: He flared up at the criticism and left his seat.
Don't snap over trivial things; just laugh them off.

examples.ko: 사장님은 실수를 지적받자 발끈하며 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: The boss snapped angrily when his mistake was pointed out.
When I asked about her age, she bristled.

explain: '화내다'가 화를 표현하는 일반적인 말이라면 '발끈하다'는 별것 아닌 말에 갑자기 욱하고 반응하는 느낌이 있어요. 오래 화를 내기보다 순간적이고 짧아요. 소리를 지르며 화내는 것은 '버럭 화를 내다'라고 해요.
explain_en: If '화내다' is the general word for getting angry, '발끈하다' is a sudden, short flare of reaction to a minor remark. Yelling in anger is '버럭 화를 내다'.
